Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Las Vegas NV
402 AM PST Wed Nov 18 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* A low pressure system will bring snow to the mountains of Inyo 
  County and southern Nevada beginning today and continuing 
  through Friday morning. 

* This low pressure system will also bring gusty southerly-to-
  southwesterly wind to the region over the next few days.

* There will be a brief reprieve from unsettled weather over the
  weekend before the next system impacts the area early next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...through Tuesday.

Early morning infrared and water vapor satellite imagery shows a cut-
off low digging along the coast of northern California. This system 
will continue to dig south, gradually pushing inland over the next 
few days, bringing unsettled weather to southeastern California, 
southern Nevada, and northwestern Arizona today through Friday. The 
Sierra will intercept the bulk of the moisture associated with this 
system, resulting in heavy mountain snow in Eastern Sierra where a 
Winter Storm Warning remains in effect through early Friday morning. 
Some moisture will manage to make it over the Sierra, bringing a 
couple inches of snow to the White Mountains of Inyo County where a 
Winter Weather Advisory remains in effect through early Friday 
morning. Rain and snow showers will begin to push into southern 
Nevada later this afternoon with a dusting of snow for elevations 
above 6,000 feet across the southern Great Basin and a couple inches 
of new snow accumulations for elevations above 7,000 feet. Further 
south in the Spring Mountains of southern Nevada, a Winter Weather 
Advisory is in effect from 4:00 am PST Thursday morning through 
early Friday morning. For elevations between 7,000 and 9,500 feet in 
the Spring Mountains, storm total snow accumulations of 3 to 9 
inches are expected. Looking specifically at the Mount Charleston 
and Lee Canyon areas, 4 to 8 inches of snow looks to be the most 
likely scenario with a 10% chance of seeing 10 inches of snow. While 
showers are expected to favor areas of higher terrain, light-to-
moderate rain showers will be possible in the lower elevations and 
valleys of southeastern California, southern Nevada, and 
northwestern Arizona as this system moves through over the next few 
days.

In addition to mountain snow, this system will also bring gusty 
southerly winds to the region today and tomorrow. 20 to 30 mph 
southerly winds with gusts to 45 mph will pick up across the 
northwestern portions of our forecast area later this afternoon, 
continuing through Thursday morning. Currently, there a Wind 
Advisory is in effect from 4:00 pm PST this afternoon through 
Thursday morning for the Owens Valley, Death Valley, Esmeralda 
County, central Nye County, southern Nye County, northern Clark 
County, and the Spring Mountains. Expect difficult driving 
conditions for high profile vehicles, and use extra caution when 
driving as blowing dust near dry lakebeds may result in visibility 
reductions. Another round of southerly-to-southwesterly winds will 
pick up across the Mojave Desert late Thursday afternoon through 
early Friday morning as the base of the trough swings through. 

Conditions will improve throughout the day on Friday into Saturday 
as the trough exits the region. While temperatures will remain 
cooler than normal through the weekend, we will have a brief 
reprieve when it comes to precipitation and winds as weak, transient 
ridging will set up across the area. This weekend reprieve will be 
brief as another system looks to impact the region early next week. 

&&

.AVIATION...For Harry Reid...For the 12Z Forecast Package...
Light and variable winds continue through the morning hours, 
becoming ENE around 8 kt after 17z. Expect winds to veer toward the 
ESE by 21z with sporadic gusts to 15 kt through sunset. Light and 
variable winds return after 02z, favoring a NW direction after 08z 
and remaining under 5 kt. Scattered mid and high clouds will become 
more prevalent beyond 00z Thursday as a storm system approaches. 
Ceilings at or below 9000ft possible after 17z Thursday as the 
chance for showers increases into the afternoon. 

For the rest of southern Nevada, northwest Arizona and southeast 
California...For the 12Z Forecast Package...Light winds expected 
through the morning hours, then expect an uptick in winds and 
increasing mid/high clouds from west to east as the next storm 
system approaches. Strongest winds today develop at KBIH around and 
after 18z with sustained winds 15-20 kt and gusts exceeding 35 kt at 
times during the afternoon. Strong southerly winds with gusts to 30 
kt continue into tomorrow night for KBIH as the chance for rain 
increases as well. Most other terminals will remain east of the 
stronger winds and rain chances, at least through 00z Thursday. Most 
sites can expect southerly winds 10 kt or less with isolated gusts 
to 15 kt during the afternoon. KDAG will be the exception as light 
and variable winds become ENE during the afternoon, then back to the 
WSW overnight tonight. 

&&

.SPOTTER INFORMATION STATEMENT...Spotters are encouraged to report
any significant weather or impacts according to standard operating
procedures.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Stessman
AVIATION...Moore

For more forecast information...see us on our webpage:
https://weather.gov/lasvegas or follow us on Facebook and Twitter
